Can i have a side hustling to pay my bills?

Yes — your skills make several practical, flexible side hustles realistic for covering bills while studying (or right after graduating in Dec 2026).

You already have strong, marketable experience in administrative support, data entry/cleaning, Excel & Google Sheets formulas, document work, Slack/Jotform setups, research, and communications. These map directly to high-demand freelance and remote work in Kenya and internationally. Many Kenyan students and recent grads earn through virtual assistance (VA), spreadsheet services, and data work.

Best Side Hustles Matched to Your CV

  1. Virtual Assistant / Admin Support (strongest fit)
    Handle inbox triage, calendar coordination, travel logistics, client communication, CRM updates, document formatting, and Slack/Jotform workflows.
    Your independent projects and church volunteer experience (media assets, event logistics) are excellent proof.
    Realistic starter rates: ~$5–10/hour (or KES equivalent on local retainers). With a few reviews and a niche (e.g., data-focused VA or real-estate/e-commerce admin), this can reach $15+/hour. Part-time (10–20 hours/week) often yields KES 20,000–60,000+ monthly once established.⁠Hustlelife
  2. Excel / Google Sheets Specialist & Data Support
    Offer data cleaning/organization (like your 500+ record Excel directory), multi-condition formulas (payroll/departmental summaries), dashboards, tracking systems, and file management.
    Clients (small businesses, NGOs, online sellers) pay for exactly the kind of work you’ve practiced. Package gigs such as “I will organize and formula-up your messy spreadsheet” or “build Google Sheets payroll summaries.”
    This pairs well with VA work and can be higher-value project-based income.
  3. Document Production, Editing & Research
    Polished business correspondence, report editing, layout consistency, online research (e.g., your ergonomic equipment project that identified savings).
    Useful for local SMEs, churches, or remote clients.

  4. Other Flexible Options

    • Online tutoring (Computer Science basics, Excel/Google Sheets, or general computer packages) — local students or platforms like Preply.
    • Data annotation / AI training tasks or transcription (good entry-level if you need quick starts).
    • Basic graphic design or event programme support (building on your church volunteer role and “basic graphic design” skill).
    • Local admin/data help for businesses, chamas, or organizations in Bungoma/Meru area (paid via M-Pesa).

Where to Find Work

  • Global platforms: Upwork (strong for VA, Excel, data entry — many Kenyan freelancers succeed here) and Fiverr (create fixed-price gigs for spreadsheet cleaning, inbox management, etc.). Freelancer.com is another option.⁠Dreamjob
  • Kenya-focused: BrighterMonday (you already have their AI Career Tool Certification), LinkedIn (optimize your profile with your projects and “open to work”), local Facebook/WhatsApp groups for VAs or remote jobs, and platforms like Kuhustle or Taskbase where available.
  • Direct outreach: Offer services to small businesses, churches, or online sellers. Your volunteer network is a natural starting point.
  • Government/digital programs: Check Ajira Digital or local Jitume ICT hubs for free training and job linkages — the government has been expanding digital job opportunities for youth.⁠Kenyanews

Practical Next Steps

  • Update/create profiles on Upwork, Fiverr, and LinkedIn today. Use your Professional Summary, Core Skills, and specific project bullets as the foundation. Add samples (even anonymized screenshots of your Excel/Sheets work or formatted documents).
  • Start with 2–3 small gigs to build reviews and testimonials. Deliver reliably and on time — this is what clients value most.
  • Set up payment methods early: Payoneer or Wise (for international clients, then to bank/M-Pesa) and direct M-Pesa for local work.
  • Treat it as a business: track time, set clear scopes, and raise rates after positive feedback. Aim for retainer clients (e.g., 10 hours/week ongoing) for more stable income than one-off tasks.
  • Balance studies carefully — schedule hustle hours around classes and prioritize high-value work.

Avoid anything asking for upfront fees or “registration payments” — those are almost always scams. Focus on legitimate platforms and verified clients.

Your combination of CS studies + proven admin/data projects puts you ahead of many pure beginners. Consistent small wins on platforms can cover bills and build experience that strengthens your full-time job prospects after graduation.

If you share more details (how many hours per week you can spare, preferred remote vs. local, or specific tools you want to emphasize), I can help refine a profile pitch, sample gig descriptions, or a starter action plan. You’ve got solid foundation — go for it.

Optimize Upwork portfolio items

Here are 4 optimized Upwork portfolio items ready to use. They are written in the strong format clients and the algorithm respond to in 2026: clear keyword-rich title → problem/goal → what you did → measurable or clear result.

1. Excel Data Organization (Strongest starter item)

Title:
Organized 500+ Record Dataset into Searchable Excel Directory with Tracking Fields

Description:
Goal: Transform a messy, unstructured list of 500+ records into a clean, searchable Excel directory that the team could filter, sort, and update easily.

What I did:

  • Standardized formatting across all columns (names, dates, categories, status).
  • Added consistent tracking fields (status, last updated, owner, notes).
  • Applied filters, data validation, and basic conditional formatting for quick visibility.
  • Ensured the file was easy to maintain and share.

Result:
Delivered a fully organized, professional Excel directory that eliminated manual searching and reduced lookup time significantly. The client could now filter and track records in seconds instead of scrolling through raw data.

(Upload: Before/after screenshots of the spreadsheet + a short note on the structure)

2. Google Sheets Formulas & Summaries

Title:
Built Multi-Condition Google Sheets Formulas for Payroll & Departmental Summaries

Description:
Goal: Eliminate repetitive manual calculations for payroll and departmental reporting by creating automated multi-condition formulas in Google Sheets.

What I did:

  • Designed and tested multi-condition formulas (SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, IF, and related functions).
  • Built clean summary sections for totals by department, category, and period.
  • Organized the sheet for easy ongoing use and future expansion.
  • Ensured formulas were accurate, documented, and protected where needed.

Result:
Reduced repetitive calculations dramatically. The team could generate accurate payroll and departmental summaries with a few clicks instead of hours of manual work. Formulas remained reliable for repeated use.

(Upload: Screenshots of the formula cells + summary tables + a brief explanation of the logic)

3. Budget Research & Savings Analysis

Presented a concise research summary that identified potential savings of up to 46% while still meeting quality and ergonomic requirements. The client received actionable options ready for decision-making.

YES

Yes! Here’s the exact step-by-step guide to put your website live on GitHub Pages for free (it will give you a link like https://yourusername.github.io).

Step-by-Step: Host Your Website on GitHub Pages

1. Create a GitHub account (if you don’t have one)

  • Go to https://github.com
  • Sign up with your email

2. Create a new repository

  1. Click the + icon (top right) → New repository
  2. Repository name:
    yourusername.github.io
    (Replace yourusername with your actual GitHub username.
    Example: if your username is calistuswaswa, name it calistuswaswa.github.io)
  3. Make it Public
  4. Check the box Add a README file
  5. Click Create repository

3. Upload your website

  1. Inside the new repository, click Add file → Upload files
  2. Drag and drop your index.html file (the one I gave you)
  3. Scroll down and click Commit changes

4. Enable GitHub Pages

  1. In your repository, click the Settings tab
  2. On the left sidebar, click Pages
  3. Under Source, select Deploy from a branch
  4. Branch: choose main
  5. Folder: / (root)
  6. Click Save

5. Wait 1–2 minutes

Your website will be live at:

https://yourusername.github.io

(Example: https://calistuswaswa.github.io)

Important Tips

  • Make sure the file is named exactly index.html (not Index.html or website.html)
  • After uploading, wait 1–3 minutes and refresh the page
  • You can update the site anytime by uploading a new version of index.html
